titre: Exercices — Structures complexes : causatif, emphase, inversion
consigne: Cherche chaque exercice au brouillon avant d'ouvrir le corrigé.

exercices.enonce: Transforme en causatif : « A mechanic is repairing my brakes. → I ___ . »
corrige: Faire faire → have + objet + PP.
I am having my brakes repaired.
exercices.reponse: I am having my brakes repaired.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Je vais me faire couper les cheveux demain. »
corrige: Causatif have/get + objet + PP.
I'm going to have/get my hair cut tomorrow.
exercices.reponse: I'm going to have my hair cut tomorrow. (I'm going to get my hair cut est aussi accepté)

exercices.enonce: Explique la différence : « I cleaned my windows. » vs « I had my windows cleaned. »
corrige: La 1re : c'est moi qui ai nettoyé.
La 2nde : je les ai fait nettoyer par quelqu'un d'autre (causatif).
exercices.reponse: I cleaned = je l'ai fait moi-même ; I had my windows cleaned = je les ai fait nettoyer.

exercices.enonce: Mets « Sarah » en relief : « Sarah sent the email. → ___ »
corrige: Clivée It + be + élément + who.
It was Sarah who sent the email.
exercices.reponse: It was Sarah who sent the email.

exercices.enonce: Mets l'objet en relief avec What : « I need a break. → ___ »
corrige: Clivée What + sujet + verbe + be.
What I need is a break.
exercices.reponse: What I need is a break.

exercices.enonce: Renforce l'affirmation : « I like this idea (insistance). → ___ »
corrige: Emphase avec do + base verbale.
I do like this idea.
exercices.reponse: I do like this idea.

exercices.enonce: Réécris avec inversion : « I have never eaten such a good meal. → Never ___ »
corrige: Never en tête → inversion sujet/auxiliaire.
Never have I eaten such a good meal.
exercices.reponse: Never have I eaten such a good meal.

exercices.enonce: Réécris : « He didn't just apologise; he also paid for the damage. → Not only ___ »
corrige: Not only en tête → inversion, avec did car pas d'auxiliaire.
Not only did he apologise, but he also paid for the damage.
exercices.reponse: Not only did he apologise, but he also paid for the damage.

exercices.enonce: Réécris sans if : « If you had told me earlier, I would have come. »
corrige: Inversion du type 3 : Had + sujet + PP.
Had you told me earlier, I would have come.
exercices.reponse: Had you told me earlier, I would have come.

exercices.enonce: Traduis avec inversion et causatif : « À peine avais-je fait réparer ma voiture qu'elle est retombée en panne. »
corrige: « à peine ... que » → No sooner had I ... than / Hardly had I ... when.
« fait réparer » → causatif had my car repaired.
No sooner had I had my car repaired than it broke down again.
exercices.reponse: No sooner had I had my car repaired than it broke down again. (Hardly had I had my car repaired when it broke down again est aussi accepté)

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « J'ai fait réparer ma voiture. »
corrige: « faire réparer » : ce n'est pas moi qui répare → causatif have + objet + PP.
Au passé : had my car repaired.
exercices.reponse: I had my car repaired. (I got my car repaired est aussi accepté)

exercices.enonce: Qui a peint la maison ? « We had our house painted last year. » (a) nous-mêmes (b) quelqu'un d'autre
corrige: have + objet + PP = causatif : on a fait faire l'action.
Ce sont donc des peintres, pas nous.
exercices.reponse: (b) quelqu'un d'autre

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « C'est Paul qui a gagné. »
corrige: Clivée It + be + élément + who.
Au passé : It was Paul who won.
exercices.reponse: It was Paul who won.

exercices.enonce: Renforce l'affirmation au passé : « She warned us (insistance). → ___ »
corrige: Emphase avec did + base verbale.
warned → did warn.
exercices.reponse: She did warn us.

exercices.enonce: Repère l'erreur : « Never I have seen such a mess. »
corrige: Never en tête de phrase → inversion sujet/auxiliaire.
I have → have I.
exercices.reponse: Never have I seen such a mess.

exercices.enonce: Transforme en causatif : « A dentist is going to check my teeth next week. → I'm going to ___ . »
corrige: Faire faire → have + objet + PP.
check → checked.
exercices.reponse: I'm going to have my teeth checked next week.

exercices.enonce: Exprime une action subie avec have : « Someone stole his phone on the bus. → He ___ . »
corrige: have + objet + PP peut exprimer un événement subi.
steal → stolen.
exercices.reponse: He had his phone stolen on the bus.

exercices.enonce: Complète avec get au causatif : « She ___ (her nails / to paint) for the wedding yesterday. »
corrige: get + objet + PP, registre plus familier.
Au passé : got her nails painted.
exercices.reponse: She got her nails painted for the wedding yesterday.

exercices.enonce: Complète avec la structure have + personne + base verbale : « I'll ___ (the technician / to install) the software. »
corrige: Obtenir que quelqu'un fasse quelque chose → have + personne + BV (sans to).
have the technician install.
exercices.reponse: I'll have the technician install the software.

exercices.enonce: Mets « in Paris » en relief : « They met in Paris. → ___ »
corrige: Clivée It + be + élément + that.
It was in Paris that they met.
exercices.reponse: It was in Paris that they met.

exercices.enonce: Mets « yesterday » en relief : « I found out the truth yesterday. → ___ »
corrige: Clivée It + was + élément de temps + that.
It was yesterday that I found out the truth.
exercices.reponse: It was yesterday that I found out the truth.

exercices.enonce: Mets l'objet en relief avec What : « She wants a quiet life. → ___ »
corrige: Clivée What + sujet + verbe + be.
Le verbe be est à la 3e personne : is.
exercices.reponse: What she wants is a quiet life.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Ce qui m'inquiète, c'est le prix. »
corrige: « Ce qui... c'est » → What + verbe + is.
What worries me is the price.
exercices.reponse: What worries me is the price.

exercices.enonce: Corrige la faute : « She did warned us about the storm. »
corrige: Après le do d'emphase, on emploie la base verbale.
did warned → did warn.
exercices.reponse: She did warn us about the storm.

exercices.enonce: Réponds avec insistance pour contredire : « You don't love me! » — « But I ___ you! »
corrige: Pour contredire avec force, on emploie do + base verbale.
I do love you.
exercices.reponse: But I do love you!

exercices.enonce: Réécris avec inversion : « I have rarely heard such a beautiful voice. → Rarely ___ »
corrige: Rarely en tête → inversion sujet/auxiliaire.
Rarely have I heard such a beautiful voice.
exercices.reponse: Rarely have I heard such a beautiful voice.

exercices.enonce: Réécris avec inversion : « He seldom complains. → Seldom ___ »
corrige: Seldom en tête → inversion ; la phrase n'a pas d'auxiliaire, on introduit does.
Seldom does he complain (base verbale).
exercices.reponse: Seldom does he complain.

exercices.enonce: Corrige la faute : « Rarely he goes out on weekdays. »
corrige: Rarely en tête impose l'inversion.
Pas d'auxiliaire → on ajoute does + base verbale.
exercices.reponse: Rarely does he go out on weekdays.

exercices.enonce: Réécris avec inversion : « I had hardly arrived when it started to rain. → Hardly ___ »
corrige: Hardly en tête → inversion : had I.
On garde when pour introduire la seconde action.
exercices.reponse: Hardly had I arrived when it started to rain.

exercices.enonce: Réécris avec No sooner : « She had just left when he called. »
corrige: No sooner + had + sujet + PP … than.
Attention : No sooner va avec than, pas avec when.
exercices.reponse: No sooner had she left than he called.

exercices.enonce: Corrige la faute : « No sooner had we sat down when the phone rang. »
corrige: No sooner est toujours suivi de than.
when s'emploie avec Hardly.
exercices.reponse: No sooner had we sat down than the phone rang. (ou : Hardly had we sat down when the phone rang.)

exercices.enonce: Réécris avec Not only : « She speaks English and she also speaks Japanese. »
corrige: Not only en tête → inversion ; pas d'auxiliaire → does.
Not only does she speak English, but she also speaks Japanese.
exercices.reponse: Not only does she speak English, but she also speaks Japanese.

exercices.enonce: Réécris avec Little : « He didn't know the truth at all. → Little ___ »
corrige: Little en tête (au sens de « pas du tout ») → inversion avec did.
Little did he know the truth.
exercices.reponse: Little did he know the truth.

exercices.enonce: Réécris avec Only then : « I understood only then. → Only then ___ »
corrige: Only then en tête → inversion ; pas d'auxiliaire → did + base verbale.
Only then did I understand.
exercices.reponse: Only then did I understand.

exercices.enonce: Réécris sans if : « If I were you, I would accept. »
corrige: Inversion conditionnelle : If I were → Were I.
Were I you, I would accept.
exercices.reponse: Were I you, I would accept.

exercices.enonce: Réécris sans if : « If you should need any help, call me. »
corrige: Inversion conditionnelle formelle : If you should → Should you.
Should you need any help, call me.
exercices.reponse: Should you need any help, call me.

exercices.enonce: Réécris avec if : « Had they known about the strike, they would have taken the car. »
corrige: Had + sujet + PP en tête = If + sujet + had + PP.
If they had known about the strike…
exercices.reponse: If they had known about the strike, they would have taken the car.

exercices.enonce: Transforme avec The reason … is that : « I left because I was bored. »
corrige: The reason (why) + sujet + verbe + is that + cause.
The reason I left is that I was bored.
exercices.reponse: The reason I left is that I was bored. (The reason why I left… est aussi accepté)

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « C'est parce qu'il pleuvait que nous sommes restés. »
corrige: Clivée It + be + élément + that ; l'élément mis en relief est la cause.
It was because it was raining that we stayed.
exercices.reponse: It was because it was raining that we stayed.

exercices.enonce: Explique la différence : (a) « I have repaired my bike. » (b) « I had my bike repaired. »
corrige: (a) present perfect : c'est moi qui ai réparé mon vélo.
(b) causatif : je l'ai fait réparer par quelqu'un d'autre.
exercices.reponse: (a) je l'ai réparé moi-même ; (b) je l'ai fait réparer.

exercices.enonce: Choisis la phrase qui correspond à « On lui a cambriolé sa maison. » : (a) « He robbed his house. » (b) « He had his house burgled. »
corrige: L'action est subie : ce n'est pas lui qui cambriole.
have + objet + PP exprime ici un événement subi.
exercices.reponse: (b) He had his house burgled.

exercices.enonce: Traduis en insistant : « Il est vraiment venu, je l'ai vu ! »
corrige: Emphase sur un fait passé → did + base verbale.
He did come, I saw him!
exercices.reponse: He did come, I saw him!

exercices.enonce: Réécris en registre soutenu avec inversion : « I have never been so humiliated in my whole life. »
corrige: Never en tête → inversion sujet/auxiliaire.
Never in my whole life have I been so humiliated. (ou : Never have I been so humiliated in my whole life.)
exercices.reponse: Never have I been so humiliated in my whole life. (Never in my whole life have I been so humiliated est aussi accepté)

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Ce dont nous avons besoin, c'est de faire vérifier le toit. »
corrige: « Ce dont… c'est » → What + sujet + verbe + is.
« faire vérifier le toit » → causatif to have the roof checked.
exercices.reponse: What we need is to have the roof checked. (to get the roof checked est aussi accepté)

exercices.enonce: Repère et corrige les deux fautes : « Not only she lost her keys, but she also had her bag steal. »
corrige: Not only en tête → inversion avec did : Not only did she lose.
Causatif : have + objet + participe passé → had her bag stolen.
exercices.reponse: Not only did she lose her keys, but she also had her bag stolen.

exercices.enonce: Lis ce court message : « My laptop broke down. A technician fixed it this morning. It works perfectly now! » Résume-le en une phrase avec un causatif.
corrige: Ce n'est pas l'auteur qui a réparé l'ordinateur → causatif.
have + objet + PP au passé.
exercices.reponse: I had my laptop fixed this morning. (Exemple de réponse ; got my laptop fixed est aussi accepté)

exercices.enonce: Réécris ce texte en mettant en relief les éléments indiqués : « Marie (relief) discovered the problem. She needed more time (relief avec What). »
corrige: Clivée It + was + élément + who : It was Marie who discovered the problem.
Clivée What : What she needed was more time (accord au passé : was).
exercices.reponse: It was Marie who discovered the problem. What she needed was more time.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « À peine étions-nous rentrés que l'orage a éclaté. » (deux réponses possibles)
corrige: « À peine… que » → Hardly had we… when ou No sooner had we… than.
« l'orage a éclaté » → the storm broke.
exercices.reponse: Hardly had we got home when the storm broke. / No sooner had we got home than the storm broke. (gotten home est aussi accepté)

exercices.enonce: Réécris ces trois conditions sans if : (a) « If I had known… » (b) « If I were rich… » (c) « If you should see her… »
corrige: Type 3 : Had I known.
Type 2 avec were : Were I rich ; should : Should you see her.
exercices.reponse: (a) Had I known… (b) Were I rich… (c) Should you see her…

exercices.enonce: Lis la situation et écris deux phrases au causatif : « Before the wedding, a hairdresser did Emma's hair and a photographer took pictures of the guests. Emma organised everything. »
corrige: Emma a fait faire sa coiffure : she had her hair done.
Elle a fait prendre des photos des invités : she had pictures of the guests taken.
exercices.reponse: Emma had her hair done. She had pictures of the guests taken. (got est aussi accepté)
